tips: Lovely Greens caps peppermint essential oil at 2% of the recipe by weight, about 0.32 oz (9 g, roughly 2 tsp) per pound (454 g) of oils. Its menthol genuinely triggers cold receptors in the skin, so the lather feels cooling: keep peppermint bars away from eyes and sensitive areas, and go easy on the rate for face or kids' soap. Spearmint's limit is far lower, 0.25%, because of its carvone content.

Eucalyptus, tea tree, and rosemary essential oils can each be used at up to about 3% (0.48 oz / 13.6 g per pound of oils). When blending several herbal oils in one bar, calculate each oil's share so the combined total stays within the limits.

Skip sage essential oil in soap. The Nerdy Farm Wife excludes it from her soapmaking chart because of its many safety warnings and contraindications; clary sage (usable around 3%, 13 g per pound of oils) or a rosemary-herbal blend gives a similar note safely.

Add dried herbs fully dried and finely pulsed; the mint from a plain tea bag works perfectly. The specks decorate rather than scent the bar, and over time each fleck develops a small golden halo as its tea seeps into the surrounding soap, a signature look of herbal tea soaps.
